stories.title: Tupac murder accused told police in 2008 his nephew fired fatal shots
stories.summary: The man accused of orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur told police more than a decade later that he handed the gun used in the drive-by shooting to a passenger who then passed it to his nephew who opened fire on the rapper. Duane "Keffe D" Davis is on trial in Las Vegas, charged with one count of murder with a deadly weapon over the killing of the rap superstar in 1996. On Thursday jurors heard a recording of a police interview with Davis in 2008. Prosecutors allege that although Davis did not fire the gun that killed Shakur, he ordered the shooting and supplied the deadly weapon to further criminal conduct for the gang he helped lead. Davis, 63, has pleaded not guilty. His lawyer Michael Sanft has argued that what his client had previously said of his involvement cannot be believed. Shakur's murder is a cold case that has gripped the public's fascination for 30 years. Prosecutors allege Davis planned the 7 September 1996 shooting after his nephew Orlando Anderson was involved in a fight with Shakur in Las Vegas hours earlier. They argue that Davis believed the attack on his nephew could not "go unanswered". Central to the case are testimonies by Davis in the formerly secret 2008 police interview and, later, in a 2019 memoir he co-authored called Compton Street Legend. Prosecutors on Thursday played the 2008 interview Davis conducted with Los Angeles. stories.title: Russian drone attack on busy shopping centre kills 14 in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy slams ‘cynical and despicable’ attack on his hometown of Kryvyi Rih that injured over 120. Russian drones have hit a busy shopping centre in the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, killing at least 14 people and wounding more than 120. Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the Kryvyi Rih Defence Council, said on Telegram that Friday’s strikes targeted the city’s largest shopping complex, sparking a fire. The death toll as of 8pm local time (17:00 GMT) was 14, with 121 injured, including 22 children. Vilkul said 29 of those injured were in critical condition. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the attack on his hometown as “cynical and despicable”. He said a second Russian drone hit the shopping centre 30 minutes after the first, in what he claimed was a deliberate attempt to target emergency services. “Attacks like these are nothing less than terrorist acts,” Zelenskyy said on Telegram, urging the world to hold Russia to account. “The world must respond to them accordingly – with real pressure on the aggressor. For peace to be possible, Russia must face real accountability,” he added. Videos on social media showed rescuers rushing to help the wounded on the street outside, as smoke billowed from the building. Meanwhile, a separate Russian strike in the Mykolaiv region killed four people, including three children, the country’s Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said.

stories.title: Dog warning as suspected palm oil washes up on beach
stories.summary: Dog owners have been put on alert after suspected palm oil washed up on a Merseyside beach. Lumps of the waxy substance were located on Egremont beach in Wirral after reports to Wirral Coastguard Rescue Team. Palm oil is widely used in the food industry but when dumped at sea it can become toxic. The coastguard said dogs could be attracted to the smell and might try to eat it - and if it was ingested it could cause a fatal reaction. Rescue officers attended the beach earlier and located a number of lumps of the substance along the beach. Some of the larger pieces were bagged and removed from the beach for collection and disposal by Wirral Council. The coastguard said: "Please take extra care when walking dogs on the beach over the next couple of days. "Further pieces may still be present or could wash ashore with subsequent tides. "Keep dogs and children away from any unusual waxy or oily substances and avoid handling them with bare hands." In January 2020, the National Trust issued a warning when a dog died after eating palm oil on Formby beach in Sefton. stories.title: Congress of Industrialists, BRICS Innovation Center sign cooperation agreement
stories.summary: According to experts, the opening of an ICIE representative office at the BRICS Innovation Center in Xiamen in 2027 will mark a significant step in the development of Russian-Chinese economic cooperation
article_sentences: PETERSBURG, August 21.

The International Congress of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs (ICIE) and the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center (Xiamen, China) have signed a cooperation agreement in principle, the ICIE press service told TASS.
"The agreement opens a new chapter in the development of business ties between Russia and China.

The parties agreed to establish a permanent representative office of the ICIE at the BRICS Innovation Center in Xiamen in 2027, as well as to jointly draft a comprehensive memorandum of understanding to formalize a long-term strategic partnership," the press service said.

The document was signed following a strategic working session attended by representatives of the Russian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs, the Russian Direct Investment Fund, and the Russia-China Investment Fund.

According to experts, the opening of an ICIE representative office at the BRICS Innovation Center in Xiamen in 2027 will mark a significant step in the development of Russian-Chinese economic cooperation.
As part of this cooperation, plans are also in place to establish a Russian-Chinese center for the protection of the rights of industrialists and entrepreneurs based at the BRICS Innovation Center.

This entity will focus on the pre-trial resolution of commercial disputes, legal support for businesses, and investment protection, serving as a reliable pillar of support for entrepreneurs operating in the Chinese market.
